Paragraph:
Translation: Then Bhisma, the great valiant grandsire of the Kuru dynasty, the grandfather of the fighters, blew his conchshell very loudly like the sound of a lion, giving Duryodhana joy.

Purport: The grandsire of the Kuru dynasty could understand the inner meaning of the heart of his grandson Duryodhana, and out of his natural compassion for him he tried to cheer him by blowing his conchshell very loudly, befitting his position as a lion. Indirectly, by the symbolism of the conchshell, he informed his depressed grandson Duryodhana that he had no chance of victory in the battle, because the Supreme Lord Krsna was on the other side. But still, it was his duty to conduct the fight...
Situation/Problem_Faced: Bhisma, the elder general, senses Duryodhana's profound internal terror and depression beneath his diplomatic posturing. He acts to temporarily alleviate his grandson's psychological distress.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Bhisma blows his conchshell loudly to project strength and provide a momentary morale boost to Duryodhana, acting out of familial affection and duty, despite knowing their side is fundamentally doomed.
Outcome/Resolution: Duryodhana experiences a fleeting moment of joy and reassurance, though the underlying reality of their impending defeat remains unchanged.

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Karuna (Compassion toward a suffering individual, even a misguided one)
Moha (Bhisma's attachment to his family/throne compelling him to fight despite knowing it is against dharma)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: This verse illustrates the tragedy of misplaced duty. Bhisma embodies immense power and compassion, yet because he is bound by worldly obligations (attachment to the Kaurava throne), he uses his strength to temporarily comfort adharma (Duryodhana) while knowing it is ultimately a lost cause against the divine will.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: Bhisma acts as an emotional regulator for Duryodhana. Recognizing Duryodhana's escalating panic attack, Bhisma uses a sudden, loud, and confident sensory input (the conchshell) to snap him out of his spiraling thoughts. It is an act of palliative care for a deteriorating psychological state.
